Mr. Mostafa Neaz Mahmud with Dr. Mohammad Abul Bashar, Advocate ------- For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Shoheb Ahmed Chowdhury with Mr. Syed Anwar Hossain. Advocate ------- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Tobarak Ali Bepari
Vs.
Hachen Kha Being Dead His Heirs 1(A) Razzak Kha and Others
full_judgment:
Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed, J: Supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner today be treated as part of the main revisional application.

2. The Rule was issued at the instance of the preemptee on the following terms:

"Let the records he called for and a Rule issue calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the order dated 31.1.1976 passed by the learned District Judge, Faridpur in Misc. Appeal No. 138 of 1975 affirming that of Mr. M.A. Jalil Munsif, Sadar Faridpur passed on 16.7.1975 in Misc. Case No. 4 of 1971 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

3. The case of the preemptor in thort is that the preemptee-opposite party purchased plot No. 486 and 510 by a registered kabala dated 24.9.1970 at a consideration of Tk. 1,500.00. The preemptor is holding land in plot no. 487 and 488 to the contiguous north of the case land. The preemptor petitioner further stated that the opposite party no. 2 sold the land to the opposite party no. 1 collusively and no notice of transfer has been served upon the preemptor petitioner and after obtaining the certified copy on 31.12.1970 the petitioner came to know about the sale finally and filed the preemption case depositing consideration money along with 10% compensation. The petitioner further stated that there is no impediment in getting the preemption as he has no land more than 10 acres.

4. The opposite party no. I preemptee contested the preemption case by filing written objection stating inter alia that the petitioner has got no cause of action for filing the preemption case and he has also no locus standi for filing preemption case. The case is barred by limitation and that the preemption case is bad for defect of parties and stated further that the application is not maintainable as per section 88 and 90 of the E.B. S.A. & T Act. The opposite party further stated the purchased the land within the knowledge of the pre-emptor petitioner and after purchase the petitioner filled up case land at a cost of Tk. 600/- by purchasing earth from Nuruzzaman and in improving the low lying land, the preemptee spent Tk. 2,000.00 and finding such position of land, the preemptor for illegal gain has filed this preemption case on some false plea and that pre-emptee hailed from Barisal and upon purchasing the land and making development of the same has constructed dwelling houses and the pre-emptee-petitioner has been residing therein with his family members and he has no other land other than this property, on the other hand, the preemptor owns substantial land and as such, he sought dismissal of the preemption case.

5. On examination of the record, it reveals that initially the preemption case was disallowed by the Trial Court by order dated 31.12.1973 mainly on the ground that there were 11 persons recorded in R.S khatian no. 156, Exhibit. B(1), Hot no. 485 lying to the north of one of the case plot no. 486 namely Kishore Mohan Nath and the others who were not impleaded as parties although names and particulars were supplied by the pre-emptee.

6. The preemptor having been dissatisfied with the order of the Trail Court preferred appeal before the District Judge, Faridpur. After hearing the parties the appeal was lowed and the pre-emption case was remanded to the Trial Court for trial afresh on fresh evidence giving opportunity to the parties.

7. After the remand, the Trial Court after hearing the parties on examination of the evidence and records allowed the preemption case by judgment and order dated 16.7.1975 in Misc. Case No. 4 of 1971.

8. The pre-emptee, thereafter, being dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the Munsif, (as it was then) preferred appeal before the District Judge, Faridpur being Misc: Appeal No. 138 of 1975. The Appeal was heard by District Judge himself after hearing the parties and considering the materials on record and also considering the judgment of the Trail Court affirmed the judgment and order of the Trial Court, thereby, preemption was allowed by the District Judge.

9. The pre-emptee being dissatisfied further with the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court filed this revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule as stated above.

10. Mr. Mostafa Neaz Mohammad, the learned Advocate along with Dr. Mohammad Abul Basher has taken me through the judgments of both the courts below and during the argument, the learned Advocate also has taken me through the preemption application and evidence of the parties and submitted having regard to the judgments of courts below that the pre-emptor-petitioner as of necessity has to prove his own case and he can not succeed on the weakness of the pre-emptee opposite party. Then, Mr. Neaz referring to the exhibits of the pre-emptor has submitted that the preemptor has failed to prove his title as being owner of the land contiguous to the case land but the courts below without adverting to the materials have allowed the preemption which is an error of saw and as such, the judgments are liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the courts below had to decide the title of the preemptor Over his own land in as much as the preemptor has not filed any documents of his tittle but he sought the preemption only submitting S.A. Khatian which has got no evidentiary value though C.S. and R.S. Khatian has evidentiary value and failing to consider those aspects of the case and allowing the preemption committed fundamental error of law. He submitted further the Courts below relying merely on S.A. Khatian without prove of title on the basis of any legal documents have allowed the pre-emption case and thus committed error of law. Mr. Mostafa Neaz Mohammad then referring to the evidence of PW. 1 submitted that one Kalu has not been impleaded in the preemption proceeding and as such, the preemption proceeding suffers from defect of parties and in spite of such materials on record the courts below allowing preemption have committed error of law and thereby, judgments are liable to be set aside.

11. Mr. Neaz Mohammad to support his contention has referred to decision in the case of Halima Begum and others Vs. Syed Ahmed and others reported in 21 DLR 854, their lords' hips observed in paragraph no:-

‘‘5. Mr. Md. Jani Alam, leaned Advocate appearing on behalf of the pre-emptor opposite party no. 1 submits that the State Acquisition Khatian having recorded the disputed land in the name of the pre-emptor it should be presumed that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in respect of the said disputed land. After what we have stated above with regard to the documentary as well as oral evidence we are unable to attach any importance to the said record of right. It is true that record of right indicates certain right of certain parties but that right is certainly dependent on some material evidence, oral and documentary so as to establish title in favour or persons who claim under the said record of right. The presumption of correctness as to C.S. record of right is not certainly available with regard to the State Acquisition Khatians. There is no. presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of C.S. Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bangal Tenancy Act."

12. Mr. Neaz then has placed the provision of section 96 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act:-

"In an application made under sub-section (1) by a co-sharer tenant or co-sharer tenants, all other co-sharer tenants of the holding and the transferee shall be made parties; and in such an application made by a tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred, all the co-sharer tenants of the holding and all the tenants holding lands contiguous to the land transferred and the transferee shall be made parties."

and submitted that holders of land contiguous to the land transferred has not been made party in the preemption case but the courts below allowing pre-emption case have committed error of law. Mr. Neaz further is trying to impress taking to the statement of the preemption application itself to the effect:

‘‘নালিশী ৪৮৬/৫১০ দাগের জমির লাগ উত্তরে দরখাস্ত কারীর সত্য দখলীয় ৮১নং সমসপুর মৌজার ঝ.অ. ২০৪ নং খতিয়ানের ১। আনা জমার অন্তর্গত ৪৮৭ দাগের ২৯ শতাংশ জমি এবং ঐ মৌজার ঝ.অ. ২০২ নং খতিয়ান ॥. আনা জমার অন্তর্গত ৪৪৮ দাগের .২৫ শতাংশ জমি থাকায় দরখাস্তকারী লাগ পাশাইলা হিসাবে" on such statement filed this pre-emption case but not a scrap of paper showing his title filed before the courts but only filed S.A. Khatian in as much as he submitted that the S.A. Khatian is not a deed of title but only such Khatian proves the possession and that S.A. Khatian has no presumption in evidence but the courts below having not recorded any findings as to the title of the pre-emptor have allowed the pre-emption on the basis of S.A. Khatian and allowing pre-emption have committed error of law.

Mr. Basher with the leave of the court at the time of pronouncement of the judgment has referred ordinance no. 10 of 1984 and placed section 6 (Chapter 4):

"section 6. No eviction, etc, from homestead.- Any land used a homestead by its owner in the rural area shall be exempted from all legal processes, including seizure, distress, attachment or sale by any officer, court or any other authority and the owner of such land shall authority and the owner of such land shall not be divested or dispossessed of the land or evicted therefrom by any means:

Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to the acquisition of such homestead under any law."

and submitted that the pre-emptee petitioner admittedly has been living on the case land and the same being homestead in the rural area has been exempted from all legal processes including seizure, distress attachment or sale by any officer, court or any other authority and the owner of such land shall not be divested or dispossessed of the land or evicted therefrom.

13. Mr. Shoheb Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Syed Anwar Hossain, Advocate has placed the judgments of the courts below, preemption application under section. 96 of SA &T Act and section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and submitted that admittedly, the preemption case was disallowed at first: The pre emptor thereafter, preferred Appeal before the District Judge, Faridpur. The Appellate Court after hearing the parties remanded the case to the Trial Court for holding trial afresh. Thereafter, the preemptor petitioner amended the preemption application adding o party no. 9 Dherandra Nath Roy alias Kalu Roy. The learned Munsif after remand, upon hearing the parties afresh had considered all aspects of the case and upon examination of the evidence and records held that the preemptor is a co-sharer tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred and further held that the case had not suffered from defect of parties. The learned Munsif also considered the development made by the pre-emptee and granted compensation and thereby, considering all the material aspect of the case had allowed the preemption thereby, committed no error of law and the Appellate Court also considered the judgment of the Trial Court as well as evidence both documentary and oral to its proper perspective and recorded proper findings that the pre-emptor is a tenant holding lands contiguous to the land transferred and the case is not barred by defect of parties and affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court and in the process, the Appellate Court passed the judgment having regard to the order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby, committed no error of law and as such, calls for no interference by this Hon'ble Court in revision. He further submitted that the facts having been resolved by the courts below concurrently, it does not warrant interference by this Hon'ble court.

14. Mr. Shoheb Ahmed Chowdhury in his reply to the submissions of Mr. Neaz Mohammad has shown from the record that Kalu had already been made party by amendment and in this view of the matter the preemption does not suffer from defect of parties and that point of law has been resolved by concurrent findings of the courts below and on this aspect, there is nothing to be interfered by this Hob'ble Court in revision.

15. Mr. Shoheb Abmed Chowdhury referring to the exhibit-B(2) and exhibit-B(3) submitted that the name of the predecessor Sonaullah Molla of the pre-emptor and the name of the pre-emptor are appearing in those exhibits marked on behalf of the pre-emptee and those are the basis of title of the preemptor and considering those exhibits the courts below held that the preemptor is a tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred and committed no error of law.

16. Mr. Chowdhury has referred to the decision in the case of Shamsul Hoque and others Vs. Moze Ali Mollah and others reported in 4 BLC 178. Their Lordships observed:

"9. Admittedly, both the S.A. Khatians as well as RS Khatians in respect of the suit land stand in the names of the predecessor-in interest of the plaintiff-opposite parties and also in some of their names It is true that the SA records, in view of section 19(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act do not provide conclusive evidence as regards title but it provides conclusive evidence as regards their preparation and revision. But entries in the SA records; in my opinion, provide a prima facie evidence as regards title. In order to maintain a suit for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the plaintiff is required to have prima facie evidence showing that he has a legal character or right to a property in respect of the subject matter of the suit and granting or refusal to grant a decree in such suit shall always depend on final adjudication thereof on evidence. Since the SA records vide Exts. 3 and 3(ka) stand in the names of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff opposite parties and also in some of their names it should be taken to be a prima facie evidence of title of the plaintiff-opposite parties in respect of the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff-opposite parties were competent to file the present suit. I do not dispute the legal principles deduced in the aforesaid cases cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners. Since the present suit was not for a declaration of title but for a declaration of the act of the revenue authority namely, the order of mutation outside the purview of law as illegal the same is certainly maintainable. Reference may be made in this connection to the case reported in 16 DLR 298."

17. I have perused the judgment of both the courts, Admittedly, the judgment of the Appellate Court is in the affirmation of the Trial Court and the courts below held that the preemption case is maintainable and that the preemptor is a holder of land contiguous to the land transferred and the courts below have arrived at such findings and decisions upon consideration of the materials on record. Be that as it may. I have considered the section 96 and sub-section 1 and 2 and upon close consideration of the provisions of the aforesaid section, it appears to me that the court has to decide only upon inquiry whether the applicant is a co-sharer tenant of the holding and in this case, the courts below have found on the basis of the S.A. Khatian that the preemptor is holding land contiguous to the land transferred. It appears further that From the records that the name of the predecessor Sonaullah Molla of the petitioner appears in R.S. Khatian which has been exhibited by the preemptee as exhibit-B(2) and so also the name of the petitioner Hachan Kha appears in exhibit-B(3). R.S. Khatian has got evidentiary value and considering the exhibits along with S.A. Khatians, exhibits 2 and 2(a) the courts below held that the pre-emptor is a tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred, taking as a prima facie evidence of title of the preemptor and the courts below allowing pre-emption on the basis of such evidence on record committed no error of law.

<u>18. In deciding the case under section 96 of the SA&T Act the courts need not make inquiry in respect of the title of the preemptor but only require to consider incidentally whether the pre-emptor is a co sharer tenant by inheritance, by purchase and tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred and in this case the courts below were satisfied that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer holding land contiguous to the land transferred on the basis of S.A. Khatians exhibit-2 and 2(a) along with the R. S. Khatian exhibit-B(2) and B(3) the courts below have committed no error of law. I find no substance in the submissions of Mr. Neaz Mohammad.</u>

19. In the facts and circumstances of the case the provision of the Ordinance No. 10 of 1984 does not have any application in the proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the contention of Mr. Bashar fails.

20. In the light of the above submissions, of the learned Advocates. I have on further consideration of the materials on record and the findings of the courts below, I am of the view that the courts below committed no error of law in allowing the preemption in favour of preemptor.

21. In the premises, I find no merit in the Rule and thereby, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs and the judgments and orders allowing preemption by the courts below are affirmed.

22. The pre-emptee will be at liberty to remove the structures at his own cost as held by the courts below within 3(three) months from the date of information given by the Trial court on receipt of the order and the pre-emptee may withdraw the consideration money along with the compensation, so deposited by the preemptor.

23. Send down the lower courts records immediately.

End.
